newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MAGGERT LEADS U.S. OPEN AS RAIN HALTS THIRD ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MAGGERT LEADS U.S. OPEN AS RAIN HALTS THIRD ROUND.

text.p: Jeff Maggert took the U.S. Open lead away from Tom Lehman on Saturday but the championship's second consecutive weather delay meant that the third-round leader would not be decided until Sunday morning.

Maggert caught Lehman, the second-round leader, with four birdies in a flawless front-nine and then held on to a tenuous one-shot advantage as all his rivals struggled on a long, wet golf course after a two-hour rain delay late in the afternoon.

While all the players had problems in the soggy conditions and fading light, the one who stumbled the worst was young Tiger Woods, who showed little of the magic that won him the Masters in record fashion in April.

Woods ended his long, frustrating day with four bogeys over the last five holes he played to stand eight shots behind Maggert going into the 17th hole, which he would have to play at 7 o'clock (1100 gmt) Sunday morning.
Maggert bogeyed one of the five holes he played after the two-hour suspension of play.

He ended the day on Congressional Country Club's 14th hole one ahead of Lehman and two better than Colin Montgomerie -- who recovered from a disastrous second round to get back into contention in his favourite tournament.

Veteran Hal Sutton, who scored an extremely rare eagle at Congressional, Tommy Tolles and young Stewart Cink were all at one under par as the Open, like usual, turned into a tight race with plenty of contenders.
Twenty-one players were still on the course when play was suspended for the day due to darkness.
